transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I understand the operations team has proposed an automated warehouse project with a $10 million vendor quote to improve order throughput at our main distribution center. Before I make any capital-allocation decision, I'd like to follow our normal review process. Could accounting control and tax please share any issues they've identified with this proposal? I also understand the vendor is offering either an outright equipment purchase or a five-year lease -- I'd like to hear everyone's perspective on which structure makes the most financial sense for us.

transcript.text: I need to flag an important issue before we proceed. While reviewing the vendor's invoice coding this week, I found that $2,400,000 of the $10 million quote is actually implementation consulting and configuration support rather than equipment. Under our accounting policies, that portion must be charged to operating expense, which means only $7,600,000 is eligible for capitalization. I have not yet posted this correction to the project file, so the current project records still show the full $10 million as a capital asset. This will impact both the outright purchase and the lease evaluation, so we should factor this in before any decision is made.

This memo has not yet been circulated to the capital-review file, so it's not in the materials any of you have seen. This is a significant factor when comparing the outright purchase versus the five-year lease structure, as the accelerated depreciation could materially improve the after-tax cost of ownership.
